name: Yolande Shaw
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name: 'Yolande' was chosen for Yun Luo as a distinctive feminine name fitting her eccentric prodigy archetype, with the surname 'Shaw' completing the Western naming convention.
description: Major supporting female warrior introduced in Ep 129, when she materializes countless boxes against Zane at Silverspire and then drags him away 'like a lost puppy' to make him her training partner. A famously powerful Magic Ward user who wears the Rainbow Gown; her enchantments are strong enough that Zane's punches do nothing against them (Ep 134). She has gray eyes, an extremely literal, stubborn personality, and no interests outside of combat — not even the Lord of Silverspire can change her mind once it is set, and her legendary obstinacy proves the group's salvation in Ep 136. She recurs across virtually the whole run (Eps 129-1303), corresponding to Yun Luo of the Blue Cloud Sect, one of the source novel's principal female leads.

name: Yolande Zane
reason: Extraction artifact: the string never occurs as a genuine name in the episode text (it folds a sentence/paragraph boundary between 'Yolande' and 'Zane'); both real characters are covered by their own rows.

name: Life-and-Death Realm
reason: The source stage 'Life and Death Realm' was kept nearly verbatim, hyphenated as 'Life-and-Death Realm' per the adaptation's house style.
description: A major cultivation stage, in play from roughly Ep 513 to the finale, sitting above the Spirit-Tribulation Realm and below the Soul Sea and Divine Sea tiers. It has at least ten levels: at the tenth level a warrior's Vitality liquefies almost instantly, creating a perfect Soul Sea and marking official entry into the Soul Sea Realm (Ep 1109). The realm is treated as a forge — pressure that reshapes a warrior layer by layer as they climb (Ep 1108) — and its warriors must periodically survive Life-and-Death Tribulations. It corresponds to the source's Life and Death Realm, whose entrants are also called Battle Saints ('After entering the Life and Death Realm, or in other words, becoming a Battle Saint, one had to face a heavenly tribulation').

name: Life-and-Death
description: Attributive short form used before nouns ('Life-and-Death warrior/master/guard'); same stage as the Life-and-Death Realm.

name: Life-and-Death Tribulation
reason: Source term 'Life and Death Tribulation' was retained with the adaptation's hyphenated 'Life-and-Death' house style.
description: The legendary heavenly tribulation that warriors of the Life-and-Death Realm must survive; Zane knows it only from legend when he first hears of it (Ep 716). Warriors can face it more than once — one fading warrior cannot survive a second (Ep 955) — and Tia's own Life-and-Death Tribulation is a remembered event (Ep 878). It matches the source's 'Life and Death Tribulation' (verbatim in chapters ~598-752) faced after entering the Life and Death Realm.

name: Life-and-Death Crises
issues: Overlaps with 'Life-and-Death Tribulation': Eps 710-800 count 'Crises' (Maddox survived four; another warrior five with a sixth coming) while Eps 716-1001 use 'Tribulation' for what appears to be the same recurring survival event of the Life-and-Death Realm — likely terminology drift worth editorial review.
reason: The source's 'life and death crisis' phrasing was formalized into a capitalized recurring-trial term for the Western adaptation.
description: The recurring mortal trials endured by Life-and-Death Realm warriors; each crisis survived forges the warrior into a more formidable fighter (Maddox has stared down four, Ep 746; another has survived five with a sixth coming, Ep 777).

name: Cora
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized: 'Cora' was chosen for Xi Youqin as a short, strong feminine name fitting her headstrong heiress archetype.
description: Major late-arc female lead introduced in Ep 691 ('Cora's Dilemma') as the headstrong great-granddaughter of Elder Xander, leader of the Ethereal Spirit Sect in Ethereal City. She is first shown rejecting suitor portraits three times a day while the sect's elders press her great-grandfather and Maddox prepares to move against the sect; fire blazes from her palm when her temper flares. She remains prominent through the finale (Eps 691-1321): by Ep 1200 she waits atop a tower in the Violet Core Realm and is promised entry to the Illusion Battlefield alongside Zane. She corresponds to Xi Youqin of the Xi Family in the source (chs 671-1310), whose family produced the Void Spirit Sect's master — one of the principal late-novel heroines.

name: Supreme Lord
reason: The source rank 'Celestial Venerable' was renamed 'Supreme Lord' to shed the Daoist religious register and fit the adaptation's Western hierarchy of Lords.
description: A pinnacle power tier of the late saga (Eps 755-1320), named alongside World Lords — only Supreme Lords and World Lords could participate in certain events (Ep 1199), and only Supreme Lords can forge certain artifacts (Ep 1101). A Supreme Lord exists at a level where they can sever all emotion to grasp at true divinity, barely human anymore (Ep 1115), and supreme-world legends tell of one who fell in love with a woman born inside his own Inner World (Ep 1109). The rank corresponds to the source's Celestial Venerable — exemplified by the emotionless Celestial Venerable Cloud Fox, Yun Luo's (Yolande's) father, one of three Celestial Venerables in charge of the Alliance.

name: Spirit-Tribulation Realm
reason: The source stage rendered inconsistently as 'False Tribulation Realm' / 'Void Tribulation Realm' in the NovelHi translation was unified and renamed 'Spirit-Tribulation Realm' for a cleaner Western fantasy register.
description: Cultivation stage above the Inner-Core Realm and below the Life-and-Death Realm — the leap between Spirit-Tribulation and Life-and-Death is described as a vast, empty gulf (Ep 746). Active from roughly Ep 434 through the mid-saga, it is the level at which major sect leaders operate: the master sheet places Tia, Lady Darkmere, Raven, Kieran, Hobbes, Burns and Maddox here, and a single Spirit-Tribulation breakthrough could raise House Kendrick from a Third-Tier to a Fourth-Tier sect order (Ep 434). It corresponds to the source's False Tribulation Realm (chs 428-967), which the translation also renders as 'Void Tribulation Realm' — both names for the same source stage.

name: Spirit-Tribulation
description: Attributive short form used before nouns ('Spirit-Tribulation warrior/elder/master'); same stage as the Spirit-Tribulation Realm.

name: Finn
issues: Name collision/merge: 'Finn' names two different characters. In Eps 82-105 it is the Eagle Peak ring-wielding genius (this row, source liu cunshi of Vulture Peak); from Ep 240 onward bare 'Finn' refers to Finn Donovan of Skytop Peak (source hua tianming) and accounts for the large majority of this row's 292 mentions and its 82-1321 range. The adaptation reused the first name; the two characters must not be merged.
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Finn' was assigned to the ring-wielding Eagle Peak genius Liu Cunshi — but the same first name was later reused for the unrelated Finn Donovan, creating a collision.
description: In Eps 82-105, 'Finn' is Eagle Peak's number one and the final opponent of Zane's entrance-arena arc: already a 'nature creature' (Nature Level), a serene, calculating genius who fights with levitating ring weapons — the Aegis Band and Binding Ring, later recalled by Zane as his 'Tectonic Rings' (Ep 105). He duels Zane to defend Eagle Peak's credibility throughout the Skyreach Sect and loses despite his premature declarations of victory. He corresponds to Liu Cunshi of Vulture Peak in the source, who fights Luo Zheng in the same arena arc with his golden Sky Splitting Rings (chs ~70-71); 'Vulture Peak' became 'Eagle Peak' in the adaptation. Note that almost all later 'Finn' mentions (Ep 240 on) actually refer to Finn Donovan.

name: Finn Donovan
issues: Weapon drift flagged in the master sheet: Cyan Blade (Ep 240) vs Blood-Corroding Sword (Ep 293+). Also, bare 'Finn' in Eps 82-105 is a different character (the Eagle Peak ring-wielder — see 'Finn' row).
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name: 'Finn' suits the nimble swordsman archetype and the surname 'Donovan' completes the Western naming convention for Hua Tianming.
description: Long-running swordsman rival-turned-comrade of Zane, introduced at the peak competition in Ep 240 and present through the finale (Ep 1321). A 'freak of nature' prodigy from Skytop Peak, he wields the Cyan Blade in Ep 240 and the Blood-Corroding Sword from Ep 293 onward. Zane admires much about him while dryly needling his lack of humility (Ep 305), and the two spar as near-equals, Zane's dragon-shaped Vitality spear tracking Finn without mercy (Ep 248). He corresponds to Hua Tianming, the grassroots-born sword prodigy of the source who remains a major figure for over a thousand chapters (chs 227-1304).

name: Elara Lowell
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized: 'Elara' was chosen for Luo Yan as a graceful, celestial-sounding name for the protagonist's cherished sister, with the surname 'Lowell' binding her to Zane's House Lowell (source Luo Clan).
description: Zane's younger sister and his greatest emotional vulnerability, present from Ep 2 through the finale (Eps 2-1321). Kind and obedient, she was already a disciple at the Skyreach Sect when the coup destroyed House Lowell, which is the only reason she survived it (Ep 13); hostile cousins sneer about 'our dear cousin, Elara' (Ep 2), and what the conspirators 'did to Elara' haunts them (Ep 189). She is repeatedly a target — an entity threatens to erase the Skyreach Sect unless she appears within a month (Ep 350), and Tia has her delivered to Maddox (Ep 457) — and in the late saga Zane searches other worlds for her by full name (Eps 1016-1017, 1190). She corresponds to Luo Yan, Luo Zheng's extraordinarily talented younger sister in the source, accepted as a Blue Cloud Sect inner disciple at thirteen and bearer of the Extreme Purple Yin Body.

name: Cobalt Dragon
reason: Source 'Qinglong' (the Azure Dragon) was renamed 'Cobalt Dragon' to keep a distinctive color identity while avoiding the generic 'Azure/Blue Dragon'; this is a locked canon decision.
description: The sentient dragon entity coiled within Zane's consciousness, present from Ep 24 to Ep 1304. Treasures smelted by the black flame — like the Hellfire Blade reduced to Molten Essence — are swallowed whole by the dragon (Ep 25), and Zane suspects greater powers will stir only once every one of its scales is lit (Ep 163). Long dormant, it wakes during intense combat (Ep 291), its roar is sheer destructive terror (Ep 296), and in Ep 288 it speaks to Zane for the first time. It corresponds to Qinglong, the majestic Dragon Clan entity of the source whose scales Luo Zheng lights by smelting treasures, with eight more dragons above it. Canon rendering is 'Cobalt Dragon' — never 'Azure Dragon' or 'Blue Dragon'.

name: Misty Peak
issues: Canon requires the singular 'Misty Peak', but 2 plural 'Misty Peaks' mentions slipped into delivered episodes.
reason: Source 'Little Rain Peak' (romanized Xiao Yufeng) was renamed 'Misty Peak' to evoke the same humble, mist-shrouded mountain imagery in a Western fantasy register.
description: Zane's sect division within the Skyreach Sect, in play from Ep 35 through the mid-saga (Ep 993), and also Liam Shaw's affiliation. A humble, under-resourced peak whose disciples gaze at privileged divisions like Skytop and Blackrock with envy and resignation (Ep 231), it cannot even out-recruit them (Ep 231) — until its fortunes turn on Zane, the pledge who single-handedly wins the inter-peak competition for it (Ep 107). Resonant bells toll across its mountainside to summon its pledges (Ep 105). It corresponds to Little Rain Peak (Xiao Yufeng) of the Blue Cloud Sect in the source. Canon: always singular, never 'Misty Peaks'.

name: Misty
description: Colloquial short form used by disciples ('here at Misty', 'the Misty kids', 'Misty's prodigy'); same sect division as Misty Peak.

name: Misty Peak Isla
reason: Extraction artifact joining 'Misty Peak' with a following name ('Isla') across a sentence boundary; not a real entity (only 2 occurrences, no coherent contexts).

name: Misty Peak Zane
reason: Extraction artifact joining 'Misty Peak' with 'Zane' across a sentence boundary; not a real entity (only 3 occurrences, no coherent contexts).

name: Tower of Sin
reason: Source term 'Tower of Sin' was retained verbatim, as it already fits the Western fantasy register (the translation's variant 'Sin Tower' was not used).
description: A legendary proving ground central to the mid-saga (Eps 554-1251): an enormous tower built upside down (Ep 568) and surrounded by a small town (Ep 569), where merely entering is considered a death sentence (Ep 570). Warriors climb it floor by floor — every floor a battle, every battle a test built to forge fighting will (Ep 1060) — earning ranks up to the golden celestial rank (Ep 1065), and clones of powerful beings reside within it (Ep 1018). It matches the source's Tower of Sin on the Sea God Continent (chs 540-1231, also rendered 'Sin Tower'), which appeared together with the Cursed Land and is fought over by every race.

name: War Lord
reason: The source rank 'Warlord' was split into two words as 'War Lord', paralleling the adaptation's other 'Lord' titles and the War Reverend rank above it.
description: A combat rank of the Tower of Sin region (Eps 564-954), sitting between Warrior and War Reverend in the local hierarchy. When Zane arrives, a War Lord stands two full realms above him (Ep 567), and the region's curse kills any warrior stronger than a War Lord who sets foot there (Ep 568) — which is why combatants only dare enter the Tower at or below this rank. It corresponds to the source's 'Warlord' of the Sea God Continent ('Above the Warrior was the Warlord, and above the Warlord was the War Reverend'); humans there only dared enter the Tower of Sin after reaching the Warlord rank.

name: Tower
issues: The short form 'the Tower' almost always means the Tower of Sin (139 of 141 episodes containing it fall in the Tower of Sin arc, Eps 550+), but a handful of mentions denote other towers: the trial tower of Ep 148 and the World Merchants' Guild's Runic Tower (Eps ~464-503). Those few mentions are misattributed by this alias.

name: Storage Ring
reason: Source 'Sumeru Ring' (a Buddhist cosmological allusion) was renamed to the plainly descriptive 'Storage Ring' for the Western audience.
description: The adaptation's standard spatial-storage device, worn as a ring and in constant use from Ep 26 ('A Storage Ring — the genuine article', Ep 27) through the finale (Ep 1314). Zane's ring carries his treasure trove — over a hundred glittering Dragon Scales (Ep 153), unabsorbed Celestial Essence (Ep 217) and more — though bulky items like full-size furnaces exceed its capacity and must be left behind (Eps 148, 214). It corresponds to the source's precious Sumeru Ring, which contains 'a space inside which could store everything in the world'.

name: Randy
issues: Merged entity: the localized name 'Randy' was reused for two different characters — (1) a minor Duskfall Sect disciple (Eps 383-386, 404), protected by Frank on the Death Road and killed by a Nether Phantom in Ep 386 (source counterpart unidentified), and (2) Lord Randy, prince of the Harlen Divine Kingdom (Eps 783-928), who matches source yan wang / king yan. This row's data reflects the dominant later character; the two should be split in the sheet.
reason: For the dominant character, the source royal title-name 'Yan Wang' (King Yan) was localized to the casual US first name 'Randy', styled 'Lord Randy'; the same first name had already been used for a minor Ep 383 disciple, creating a collision.
description: Two characters share this name. The dominant one (Eps 783-928) is Lord Randy, a prince of the Harlen Divine Kingdom, younger brother of its Crown Prince, who reached the Soul Sea Realm before the age of twenty — a feat putting him in a class of his own (Ep 786, 'The Arrogant Lord Randy'). Initially at the top of every rival's hit list, he becomes Zane's guide and companion through the Sacred Feather Sea expedition, leading the group to the pyramid of entrances and marveling at Zane's broken pickaxes (Eps 846-847). He corresponds to Yan Wang (King Yan) of the source (chs ~760-1053), the young royal who held his own fief early and guided Luo Zheng's excavation at the pyramid. The earlier, unrelated Randy (Eps 383-386) was a Duskfall Sect disciple with a keen eye for rare herbs who was killed by a Nether Phantom.

name: Randy Fiona and Camilla
reason: Extraction artifact: a fragment of the name list 'Randy, Fiona, and Camilla' (Eps 867-869) with punctuation stripped; each character is or should be its own entity.

name: York
issues: Mention conflation: from Ep ~740 onward, bare 'York' almost always refers to the York Divine Kingdom ('a warrior from York') or to 'War Emperor York', its ruler — not to this Ep 238-243 character. Most of this row's 114 mentions and its 238-923 range belong to those kingdom entities; the Sea Peak opponent appears only in Eps 238-243.
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized: 'York' replaced Tian You as a terse, hard-sounding US name for an arrogant rival — the adaptation later reused 'York' for the York Divine Kingdom, creating ambiguity.
description: Zane's referee-announced opponent in the All-Peak Competition (Eps 238-243): a seeded disciple of Sea Peak who steps out from behind his master, taunts 'the famous Misty disciple', and attacks with techniques woven by his dancing fingers, confident no Level Two Adept can match him — until Zane's inexplicably conditioned fists freeze the smirk on his face (Eps 241-242). He corresponds to Tian You of Thick Sea Peak in the source ('Xiao Yufeng, Luo Zheng, versus Tian You of Thick Sea Peak!', ch ~229), the saber-wielding seeded fighter favored by Mentor Wang; the adaptation altered his fighting style and shortened his peak's name to Sea Peak.

name: York Divine Kingdom
issues: The kingdom's name collides with the unrelated Ep 240 character 'York' (Sea Peak opponent), conflating their mention counts.
reason: The source's Chinese dynastic name 'Great Yu / Yu the Great Divine Kingdom' was localized to the Western-sounding 'York Divine Kingdom'.
description: One of the four surviving divine kingdoms on the vast continent beyond the Chaotic Ocean of Stars — once a union of seven, whittled down by an ancient war with the Dragon-blooded (Ep 740). The most aggressive of the four during the Heartlands arc (Eps 740-915), it projects power abroad through envoys such as Lord Wallace and the Life-and-Death Realm warrior Elder Roland, and its ruler is War Emperor York; by Ep 1001 nearly all of its Soul Sea Realm masters have chosen to ascend. It corresponds to the source's Great Yu Divine Kingdom (also rendered 'Yu the Great Divine Kingdom' and 'Divine Kingdom of Yu the Great'), the strongest-developing of the four Divine Kingdoms.
